newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end unchanged in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end unchanged in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed almost unchanged in quiet trading on Wednesday as the market reached equilibrium, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): unchanged at 103.04
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: uncahnged at 102.1
Volume was low at 130 million shekels.
"The market has come to a saturation point and it has stabilised following recent gains. CPI-linked bonds were stable after several days of declines," said a trader at Tachlit Investments.

"Yields on inflation-linked bonds have fallen sharply since the beginning of the year from 4.6 percent to around 4.2 percent. During the last several days we saw a slight correction in yields but in the long run they are expected to continue rising with yields falling towards 4.0 percent," said a trader at Sahar Securities.
Unlinked bonds and Makams were also stable as investors awaited further news concerning a possible reduction of the Bank of Israel key lending rate, the Tachlit trader said.
Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly lower after the shekel rose against the dollar, the Sahar trader added.
In the local forex market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3520 shekels against 3.3590 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
